texts: bad: "after several weeks" is dropped entirely — a forward offset with no number and nothing to count from matches none of the licensed time forms (a date bound, an ordering against another stated event, a measured gap from "now", or a duration of the eventuality itself), so the parse records only that a wraith fades back into the cove, with no indication of when. Attach the span to the wraith's own persistence and order the fading against it: "A wraith persists for several weeks before it fades back into the cove." That gives "several weeks" a duration slot on the persisting and an explicit before-ordering for the fading; "several" itself still has no exact carrier and will come through as an at-least-two-weeks bound, so state a number if the exact span matters.

good. the indefinite subject stays a specific witness rather than becoming a generic rule, the participial modifiers stay unfused adjectives, and "each night" takes the named-slot plus implied-cycle pair with no quantifier companion.

mixed: everything but one atom is right, but the event noun "persistence" is typed under the verb class persist, which is barred — lemmatization is inflection-only, so a noun derived from a verb keeps its own form — and a later query about a wraith's persistence will not match. Use the finite verb instead of the deverbal noun: "A wraith drains many lanterns while it persists." "While" is one of the three words that license the two-eventuality nesting, so the during-link survives and the class symbol is now the verb's own.
